newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai dirty car owners to pay clean air tax.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai dirty car owners to pay clean air tax.

text.p: Shanghai has begun to levy an air pollution tax of between 50 yuan ($6) and 150 yuan per year on vehicles which fail an emission test, officials said on Tuesday.
Shanghai is the first city in China to levy such a tax, an official for the Bureau of Environmental Protection said.
The city has 450,000 automobiles and 150,000 motorcycles, all of which have to pass an annual inspection by the Public Security Bureau.
About 40 percent of the vehicles will have to pay the tax, the official said, but added that the operational details of the taxation system had yet to be decided.
There was no immediate indication of what the money will be used for.
There are also at least 400,000 mopeds -- bicycles with tiny engines attached -- in Shanghai and most of them must pay the tax too, he said.

Mopeds are amongst the worst polluters on the streets of Shanghai and the issuance of new moped licences was stopped by the city government earlier this year in an effort to help clean up the air. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
